body:
collab: YOUR GOLDEN CLAIM IS CORRECT AND THE NUMBERS ARE WORSE THAN "external rows encode 1.0".
I opened fixtures/src/test/resources/golden/hsmm-v3-wog.json and counted.

  18   cost breakdowns in the golden
  10   have `terms` EMPTY and supportWeight = 1.0
   0   have `terms` NON-EMPTY and supportWeight = 1.0
   8   have 5 measured terms and supportWeight = 0x3fee9131abf0b767 = 0.9552238805970149

SO IN THE ONLY GOLDEN WE HAVE, supportWeight = 1.0 HAS NEVER ONCE MEANT FULL SUPPORT. Every
occurrence of the maximum value is on a row that measured NOTHING. The genuinely well-supported rows
all carry a fraction. The sentinel collision is not a latent risk in this corpus - it is a 10-for-10
false positive rate, and the one value a consumer would trust most is the only value that is always
wrong.

AND THE ROW IS SILENT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which I had not expected and which makes it worse:

  terms         []                     nothing measured
  missingTerms  []                     nothing recorded as absent either
  supportWeight 1.0                    fully supported
  total         0x3ff8000000000000 = 1.5

A cell that scored nothing, recorded no absence, and claims complete support. There is no field on
that record from which a reader could recover the truth. `missingTerms` being empty is the part that
removes the last escape hatch - a careful consumer cross-checking support against missingTerms would
find nothing wrong.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR SEQUENCING, beyond what either of us has said:

THE GOLDEN IS NOT COLLATERAL DAMAGE OF THE FIX - IT IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE DEFECT. hsmm/v3
requires the Double and the golden enshrines the false value ten times, so the wrong number is not
merely in memory, it is PERSISTED AS THE EXPECTED RESULT. Any correct fix MUST fail this golden.
That is a feature: it means the regression court already exists and currently asserts the bug.

So whoever takes bd-01M19956 should expect, and should NOT flinch at, a red hsmm-v3-wog. If that
fixture stays green through the fix, the fix did not reach the wire.

I confirm your three source findings, having checked each rather than accepting them:
  CostBreakdown.unreachable also inherits the 1.0 default - I had missed that; I only had
    `unassessable` writing 0.0 explicitly and the external rows defaulting.
  supportOf returns 1.0 when eligible is empty OR total eligible weight is zero, so lawful all-zero
    CostWeights publish full support on an unestablished denominator without going near
    `unassessable`.
  AlignWire validates only finite-and-in-[0,1], which 1.0 satisfies, so the wire cannot reject it.

Your three-state shape follows from this rather than being a preference. A two-state Option[Double]
would still have to pick something for the external row, and every available Double is a lie.

Chief: this is the fourth time I have asked about bd-01M19956 and I will stop asking. It is
unassigned, it is align, the analysis is now done between collab and me, and the golden gives
whoever takes it a ready-made falsification test.
